sections.heading: Roof Repair, Storm Damage, or a New Roof? The 25% Rule

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: As a rule of thumb, once damage covers more than about 25% of a roof, a new roof usually beats repeated roof repair. In New Jersey, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months on a building other than a detached one- or two-family home also needs a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Below that line, roof repairs include shingle replacement and flashing repair, and asphalt roofs are easy to repair if damaged during a storm; Belleville roof repairs typically range from $300 to $5,000, per published local estimates, so roof repair cost stays a fraction of replacement. sections.heading: How to Tell If a Roofer Is Lying: Choosing Expert Roofing Contractors in Essex County

runs.v: Municipalities and states often require roofing contractors to be licensed or registered and insured; New Jersey requires home improvement contractors to register with the Division of Consumer Affairs, and the Contractors' Registration Act requires a written contract for any home improvement over $500, with three business days to cancel. A roofer may be lying when claimed damage comes with no photos, when a price is good for today only, or when the contract carries no registration number. A salesperson can seem like a great guy and promise an excellent job, excellent service, and an extremely professional crew; expert roofing contractors put the shingle line, underlayment, tear-off, and deck repair in writing instead. Quality and customer satisfaction show in that written scope and in a written workmanship warranty on the labor. sections.heading: FAQs About Asphalt Shingles for Belleville Homeowners

faqs.q: What is the difference between 3-tab and architectural shingles?

runs.v: Architectural shingles bond multiple layers of fiberglass mat into a dimensional profile that lasts 30 years and rates up to 130 mph with the manufacturer 6-nail pattern; 3-tab shingles use a single flat layer that lasts 20 years, per InterNACHI and ARMA.

faqs.q: How long do asphalt shingles last on a Belleville home?

runs.v: About 30 years for architectural and 20 years for 3-tab shingles, per InterNACHI, with actual life varying up to 40% with climate, install, and maintenance, per the NRCA; canopy debris and shade-driven moss shorten neglected Belleville homes' roofs.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for asphalt shingle roofing in Belleville, NJ?

runs.v: A complete re-roof of a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit; a commercial, multi-family, or attached building exceeding 25% of the roof area within 12 months needs one. Confirm with the Belleville construction office before work.

faqs.q: Does a historic designation restrict asphalt shingle roofing in Belleville?

runs.v: Confirm the property's local historic status with the Township of Belleville before work, since locally designated properties can need extra review. Per the National Park Service, a National or State Register listing alone places no restriction on a private property owner.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace an asphalt shingle roof in Belleville?

runs.v: Replace when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost; repair when damage stays localized on a sound roof under 10–15 years old, per contractor-consensus thresholds cited by Modernize.
